study type: Planned secondary analysis of a prospective randomized trial
exposure: Study site (Guatemala, Pakistan, Zambia, Democratic Republic of Congo)
cohort: 12,940 pregnant women in community settings in Guatemala, Pakistan, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo
finding: Oligohydramnios was associated with worse neonatal, fetal, and maternal outcomes in low and low-middle income countries.
mod_finding: Women diagnosed with oligohydramnios had higher rates of cesarean delivery compared to women without oligohydramnios.
country: Guatemala, Pakistan, Zambia, Democratic Republic of Congo
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 162 g less in infants exposed to oligohydramnios.
